clue.text: Dazed, having swallowed cigar butt and likely to croak?

indicators.note: the first piece takes the next one inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: dazed means foggy, mentally clouded

indicators.note: the butt of something is its end, so only the final letter of cigar is used

explanation.surface: Someone woozy after inhaling the end of a cigar sounds hoarse enough to croak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having swallowed' puts R, the last letter of cigar, inside FOGGY. The definition is playful: a frog croaks, so something froggy is likely to croak.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs croak, so a frog-like voice or creature is whimsically one likely to croak; froggy also means hoarse.

clue.text: Picture specialist student doctor attending university after one admitted to a succession of poor grades

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so these pieces go inside the grades

parts.note: F is a failing grade, so a run of poor grades is three Fs

indicators.note: after says the student-doctor-university group follows one
attending means accompanying, so the university comes alongside the doctor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is for learner, a student driver
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A trainee medic at university gets a run of failing marks while studying photography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means film, not a painting; F is a failing grade, so 'a succession of poor grades' is a run of them, split open by 'admitted to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A film buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge of motion pictures.

clue.text: Golden year pursuing passion fruit here

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the year comes after the passion

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
anger is a passion, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: Golden year spent chasing passion fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' looks like one thing, but 'passion' is ANGER and 'fruit here' is the definition. OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a greenhouse where orange trees and other fruit are grown, so a place where fruit grows.

clue.text: Commoner alleging bureaucrat¿s confused

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive ending adds no letters; the word is used as written

explanation.surface: A member of the public claims an official has got muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ALLEGING BUREAUCRAT. 'Commoner' is not a non-noble: the Wombles live on Wimbledon Common, and Great Uncle Bulgaria is their elder.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Uncle Bulgaria is the eldest Womble in the British children's books and TV series, living on Wimbledon Common.

clue.text: Woolworth initially invested in mouldy ragout, given struggling competition

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the initials go into the rearranged stew
something mouldy has gone off and lost its shape, so the letters of ragout are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
F. W. Woolworth, founder of the Woolworths chain of stores, had the initials F and W

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's money is sunk into a stew gone bad, prompting a fight over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolworth initially' means the founder's initials (F. W. Woolworth), not just the first letter of the name; 'mouldy' gives TUGOAR, opened by 'invested in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug-of-war is a contest of strength in which two teams struggle on opposite ends of a rope.

clue.text: See 3
"May I have your attention" admits false hope with gas pipes

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the call encloses the rest

parts.note: oi is a call to get someone's attention

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of hope with gas are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for attention concedes that hope is misplaced, along with some piping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words that 'false' scrambles; 'admits' puts the scramble inside the attention-getting shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagi are the gullets, the tubes carrying food from throat to stomach.

clue.text: Cry when Mandela's spoken

indicators.note: spoken says the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Winnie Mandela was the wife of Nelson Mandela

explanation.surface: Someone weeps when Nelson Mandela's name is uttered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandela' stands for Winnie Mandela; said aloud her name gives the horse's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinny is a horse's gentle high-pitched neigh, a kind of cry.

clue.text: Smoking jacket?

parts.note: read differently, a jacket that is one thing and something smoked another; the word names both a cannabis cigarette and a sailor's thick double-breasted coat

explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is both a cannabis joint for smoking and a thick close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Part of holiday

definitions.meaning: to part is to go away or depart
a holiday from work, as in annual time off granted by an employer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to depart from a place and a period of permitted absence from work, such as holiday.

clue.text: Relapse, left in cheeky situation

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: playfully, the place where the cheeks of the bottom are situated is the backside

explanation.surface: Someone slips back into bad habits after being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheeky situation' is a pun: the situation of the buttock cheeks, the backside, not an impudent moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into former bad ways after improvement.

clue.text: Notices location where directors have been shot?

definitions.meaning: a place where notices are pinned up
a company board of directors with a bullet in it, read whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin board is where notices are displayed; split up it describes a board with a bullet in.

clue.text: Beautiful girl carying a gun is nothing to worry about

indicators.note: carrying (spelt so in the clue) means holding within, so the girl contains the other pieces

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl or woman
gat is old slang for a gun, from Gatling

explanation.surface: A pretty girl packing a pistol is apparently no cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carying' is printed with one R but plainly means carrying: BELLE holds A GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, something of little importance and nothing to fret over.

clue.text: Bum somewhat plump on celebrity

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tabloid jibe calling a famous person a bit on the chubby side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is to cadge or scrounge it, which is also what ponce means in British slang.

clue.text: Trees — a restful sort of early offer

parts.note: firs are a kind of tree

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to arrange, so the letters of a restful are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of trees as a restful kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' looks like a hedge on 'restful', but 'sort' is the anagram signal: A RESTFUL becomes TREFUSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: First refusal is the right to accept or decline an offer before anyone else is given it, an early offer.

clue.text: Overly stupid parking installed leaves one manoeuvring into narrow space

parts.note: too means overly, excessively

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside, so parking goes into the word for stupid

parts.note: thick means stupid
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A dim driver squeezing into a tight parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed' puts P inside THICK. 'leaves' is a link meaning results in.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a small stick worked into the narrow gaps between teeth.

clue.text: Punishing course of study at poly gone to be reshaped

indicators.note: reshaped means given a new form, so the letters of poly gone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A course at a polytechnic is being revamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reshaped' rearranges POLY GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penology is the study of punishment and prison management, a course of study about punishing.

clue.text: Fiance punched in the stomach having lost head grabbing 3 and 7

indicators.note: grabbing means holding within
losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a punch to the stomach leaves one winded
three plus seven make ten

explanation.surface: A betrothed man is struck in the gut and loses his head over two other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 and 7' look like cross-references to other clues but are simply numbers adding up; 'having lost head' leaves INDED, which 'grabbing' opens.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a fiance.

clue.text: Creature from ancient China (oriental) arrested by Defence Minister's messenger

indicators.note: arrested by means held inside, so the creature and E are captured within the minister

parts.note: Geoff Hoon was the UK Defence Secretary from 1999 to 2005
a pig from the Ming dynasty, a period of ancient Chinese history
E for East, i.e. oriental

explanation.surface: A Chinese antique animal and an Easterner are detained by a government minister's courier.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on knowing Geoff Hoon, Britain's Defence Secretary when the puzzle appeared; a Ming pig is a creature from the Ming dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing pigeons were trained to fly messages back to their loft, so they served as messengers.

clue.text: Sailor rounds port having jettisoned love happily, say

indicators.note: rounds means goes around, so the sailor encloses the rest

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: jettisoned means thrown out, so the O is removed

parts.note: Dover is an English port
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A seaman sails round a harbour after cheerfully dumping his love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happily, say' defines by example: happily is one of that word class. 'having jettisoned' leaves DVER, and 'rounds' wraps the sailor about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Happily is an example of a word class that modifies verbs, as signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Minor wounds turned over, applying firm plaster

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cuts are minor wounds
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Small injuries flipped over while sticking on a plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses CUTS to give STUC. 'plaster' is not a sticking plaster but building plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and mould decorations.

clue.text: Dump the wife, if I were you

definitions.text: Dump the wife, if I were you

parts.words: Dump the wife, if I were you
parts.note: read as blunt advice to a friend: the word wanted is the one an adviser would use for getting rid of a spouse, meaning dump

explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to dump or abandon something or someone, as one might advise doing to a spouse.

clue.text: Boat song of which dog heard part

indicators.note: heard says the word for the dog's noise is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a dog's noise is a bark
a part in a play is a role, here taken as 'a role'

explanation.surface: A song from a boat, part of which you can hear a dog joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns BARK into BARC; then 'a role' for 'part' completes the sound of 'bark a role'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a song traditionally sung by Venetian gondoliers, so a boat song.

clue.text: Storyteller's revolutionary main work

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for main is read backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A writer's radical masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses SEA to AES. 'main work' looks like magnum opus, but 'main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Mixed dhal, a nice spicy dish

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lentil curry blended with something nice makes a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges DHAL A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a tortilla rolled round a filling with chilli sauce.

clue.text: Don leaves oath by which those who live also die

definitions.text: by which those who live also die

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the word for donning is taken out

parts.note: an oath can be a curse, a swear word
to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: A university don walks out on a sworn promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher but means to put on, WEAR; 'leaves' removes it from SWEARWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'those who live by the sword shall die by the sword' gives a weapon that both lives and kills by.

clue.text: Sea barrier commanded to restrict canal barrier

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command
a lock is a gated section of a canal

explanation.surface: An order to limit a canal lock creates a barrier at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea barrier' and 'canal barrier' look parallel, but only the first is the definition; 'to restrict' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade is the sealing off of a port or coast by ships, a barrier at sea.

clue.text: Reportedly, this works soil no longer fertile

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: a spade is a tool for digging and working soil

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool is said to be useless for barren ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The digging tool, SPADE, is said aloud to give the same sound as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spayed animal has had its ovaries removed, so it can no longer breed.
